criteria.title: Casing — sentence case across all product UI text
criteria.test: **Rule.** Sentence case is the house default for **all** product UI text — buttons/CTAs, menu/tab/nav items, **slide-type and interactive-component names**, headings, tooltips, dialog titles, empty states, messages. Capitalize the **first letter only**; keep proper nouns / brand names / acronyms as-is.

criteria.title: Specific — names the object + what happened
criteria.test: **Rule.** A problem message says *which* thing and *what* about it. Vague, information-free shells are banned as a standalone message: *Something went wrong · An error occurred · Oops / Uh oh · Unexpected error · Some items could not be loaded · bare Failed / Error · Invalid input*.

criteria.title: Actionable — states the next step AND exposes the recovery
criteria.test: **Rule.** Any **recoverable** problem tells the user what to do now and exposes the recovery as a real control when a one-tap recovery exists (Retry / Reload / Log in again / Go back / Contact support). An outcome with no next step is a **dead-end** — the "*so what now?*" reaction.

criteria.title: Human — blameless, jargon-free, no raw codes in the headline
criteria.test: **Rule.** Don't blame the user; keep raw error codes / stack / HTTP status out of the headline (a code belongs in secondary detail); use plain language; lead with the user's goal.

criteria.title: Proportional — severity of wording matches real impact
criteria.test: **Rule.** The words (and the type handed to the surface) match actual impact. A transient, retryable hiccup is a calm info/warning, not a blaring red "Error".

criteria.title: Empty ≠ error
criteria.test: **Rule.** An empty state ("nothing here yet") is a success with no data — encouraging, with a **primary create action**, never an apology or a red alarm. A load **failure** is never disguised as emptiness ("No presentations" when the fetch actually errored hides the Retry the user needs).

criteria.title: Right home & shape
criteria.test: **Scope.** If the surface has **no** recovery-required message and **no** title+body message at all (e.g. a labels-only surface), C7 is **`N/A`** in full — not PASS.

criteria.title: Punctuation: no em dash or en dash
criteria.test: **Rule.** Product copy never uses an em dash (—) or en dash (–) as punctuation. Use a full stop, a comma, a colon, parentheses, or split into two sentences instead.

criteria.title: Real brand identity, never a placeholder
criteria.test: The brand mark + wordmark, and any third-party brand logo, are taken from the Logo library (design.ahaslides.io/foundations/logo.html, files at /logo/<file>), never redrawn, hand-inlined, recoloured, or replaced by a coloured letter tile or initials square.

criteria.title: No dead placeholder shipped as a final state
criteria.test: Every region renders a real asset or a proper empty state — never a permanent 'Loading…' label, spinner, or grey box (e.g. a QR block shows a real code or an explicit 'code unavailable', not 'Loading QR…').

criteria.title: Deliberate hierarchy, one primary action per region
criteria.test: Each region has one clear primary action and a scannable type hierarchy from the scale; not uniform grey-on-white cards of equal weight with evenly-spaced everything.

criteria.title: Shell chrome is tokenised and reuses DS components
criteria.test: Nav rail, top bar, and content region take spacing/radius/colour from --aha-* tokens and fill their slots with DS components (aha-button, aha-icon, aha-avatar, aha-badge, DataTable), never hand-rolled buttons/icons/hex/px.

criteria.title: Active/selected nav state animates on a persistent node
criteria.test: The active nav item and any selected state toggle an attribute/class on a persistent node via motion tokens (--aha-motion-* / --aha-ease-*), never a bare duration literal and never by rebuilding the subtree.

targets.use: every shared component's live DS contract (spec, variants, sizes, states, conformance) — the target look, replacing the frozen Storybook contract.json snapshot
the colour roles and structural values the contracts bind to

criteria.title: Structural values match the measured standard
criteria.test: Radius, height, padding, gap and font family / size / weight for the component under review equal the values in its live DS contract (the <slug>.agent.json feed) — structural values are the same in every binding; any off-by value fails (e.g. radius 6px where the contract says 8px).

criteria.title: Every variant & size is covered
criteria.test: Every variant and size the live DS contract declares is implemented — none of the matrix is missing.

criteria.title: Every sub-part is styled
criteria.test: Every sub-part is styled, not just the outer box: Modal = content + header + body + action footer + close button; Dropdown = menu + item; Input = box + placeholder.

criteria.title: Every interaction state exists
criteria.test: Anything clickable has every interaction state — rest / hover / focus / active / disabled; an absent state fails.

criteria.title: Each state is rendered on the SAME property the standard uses
criteria.test: Each state is rendered on the same property the contract uses (tag active = an outline; radio checked = the tick; checkbox/toggle on = a fill; upload error = the text colour; tooltip = its theme); reproducing a state on the wrong property fails.

criteria.title: Colour is bound as a role for the right context
criteria.test: Structural values are fixed and only colours change per binding: the component uses the colour role for its context — brand (app chrome) or user/neutral (a theme-following canvas) — while danger, positive and brand-pink stay fixed in every binding, all bound to DS colour tokens.

criteria.title: Icon size / box / spacing matches
criteria.test: The icon inside a component has the size, box and spacing the contract fixes and takes the surrounding text colour; the glyph itself is the repo's own asset (exempt).

criteria.title: Verified against the reference picture, not eyeballed
criteria.test: A "matches" claim is evidenced by a screenshot of the built component compared with the DS doc-site render of that component (or the value read from its live DS contract) — not prose, not "looks right"; overlay/interactive parts are captured in their open state.

targets.use: the <aha-icon> API: on-grid sizes, currentColor/token colour, -filled state assets, accessible name
the catalogue of glyph names a view must reuse

criteria.title: One shared icon set — never mixed
criteria.test: Every glyph comes from the single shared icon component (<aha-icon name> in the DS, the shared SVG Icon in an app) and one view uses the system-* outline family consistently — never mixed with @ant-design/icons, Lucide, Heroicons, FontAwesome, Material, Phosphor in a migrated repo, a hand-rolled inline <svg>, or a legacy fill/multicolour glyph.

criteria.title: On-grid size with its paired line-width token
criteria.test: Size is one of the four on-grid values — 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 — via the icon's size prop, so the runtime draws its paired line width (12px 1px, 16px 1.5px, 24px 2px, 32px 2.5px) whatever the glyph's viewBox; never an off-grid size (no 20px) and never a hardcoded one-off stroke width. A glyph may be drawn by hand only when the library has no suitable icon, and then its stroke follows the size: 12px 1px, 16px 1.5px, 24px 2px, 32px 2.5px.

criteria.title: Emphasis via variant; colour via token, not a hardcoded hex
criteria.test: State and emphasis use the -filled glyph variant (or a colour token), never a thickened stroke; colour inherits currentColor or a semantic/brand token (--aha-icon-*, --aha-color-*), never a hardcoded hex on the icon.

criteria.title: Accessibility — labelled, tooltipped, or hidden
criteria.test: An icon-only button carries an accessible name (aria-label or an sr-only label) plus a tooltip when the glyph's meaning isn't obvious; a decorative icon that repeats adjacent text is aria-hidden; state is never conveyed by colour alone.

criteria.title: Standard catalog glyph reused, not a new inline drawing
criteria.test: Common meanings reuse the established catalogue glyph from the live icon registry (validation → warning-circle, success → check-circle, search → magnifying-glass, settings → gear, more → dots-three-vertical, add → plus) rather than a new synonym or a fresh inline drawing; a genuinely missing glyph is added to the DS library; a new drawing is allowed only when the library has no suitable icon.

criteria.title: presenter-app render mode matches the intended fill/outline state
criteria.test: In presenter-app the render mode matches the intended look: an outline-intended system-* glyph uses maintain-color (the default fill: currentColor would blob it), a filled/active glyph or *-fill / *-solid asset stays filled, colour flows through the surrounding element (there is no color prop), and a baked-in stroke hex is fixed at the asset, not with a prop.

criteria.title: A glyph matches the word it stands for
criteria.test: An icon beside a label must depict that label. Mood / sentiment labels use the face set — `system-smiley` (happy / glad), `system-sad-face` (sad), `system-angry-face` (mad / angry). FAIL when a stand-in with a different meaning is used because the right glyph seemed missing (e.g. `system-thumbs-down` for "Sad", `system-fire` for "Mad"). If the registry truly lacks the glyph, add it to the DS rather than borrowing one.

targets.use: the live type scale — font (product), weight (400/600), size, lineHeight and letterSpacing — replacing the frozen typography.json snapshot

criteria.title: Font family matches the role
criteria.test: Product UI text uses the DS product face (Plus Jakarta Sans, the font.product token) for every role; any other family (Poppins, Roboto, Helvetica, SF, Inter) fails — the live DS scale has no Inter label set.

criteria.title: Weight is 400 or 600
criteria.test: Font weight is 400 (regular) or 600 (semibold) only, per the live weight tokens — Display included; 500 / 700 / 800 on a role-based heading or body fails. Text baked into a shared component follows that component's DS contract instead.

criteria.title: Size snaps to the scale
criteria.test: Font size snaps to the DS size tokens (12 · 14 · 16 · 18 · 20 · 24 · 32 · 40 · 48 · 56 · 64); an in-between value (15, 17, 22, 28, 36…) or a rem/em that computes off-scale fails.

criteria.title: Line-height is a unitless ratio matching the role
criteria.test: Line height is a unitless ratio from the DS lineHeight tokens matching the role — 1.2 (H1/H2), 1.3 (H3–H6, blockquote), 1.5 (body, lead) or normal; a px line height, or a ratio that doesn't match the role, fails.

criteria.title: Letter-spacing matches the role's category
criteria.test: Letter spacing matches the role's category per the DS letterSpacing tokens — headlines 0 · subheadings 0.2px · paragraph 0.2px · subtext 0.3px; negative tracking on a heading fails.

criteria.title: Role fits the text's job
criteria.test: The role is chosen by the text's job, not its rough size — page title → heading1 (via <aha-breadcrumb size="page-title">); section → heading2/3; card/dialog title → heading4/5; base UI → body; caption/helper → bodySM — and the five values together match a single DS role.

criteria.title: In scope — product UI, not marketing/brand
criteria.test: The scale governs in-app product UI (presenter, audience, editor, dashboard); a marketing/brand surface (landing, blog, email, social graphic) is not forced onto it, and vice versa.

targets.use: the DS V3 DataTable — header, body, sort, filter, freeze, pagination, cell padding
the colour and radius tokens the grid binds to

criteria.title: It is the shared DataTable — not hand-rolled, not a restyled raw Table
criteria.test: The grid renders through the shared DataTable (AntD <Table> underneath); a raw <table>/<div> grid or a bare AntD <Table> with its own styling fails.

criteria.title: The look is theme-driven — no per-table styling
criteria.test: The look comes from the theme (components.Table), not the call site — a per-table bordered, size, rowClassName zebra, inline header/cell style or ad-hoc container styling fails.

criteria.title: Header is white with secondary-grey labels
criteria.test: The header is white (Table.headerBg) with secondary-grey labels (Table.headerColor) and a bottom divider — never AntD's default grey #fafafa fill, a tinted header, or default-colour labels.

criteria.title: Body has horizontal dividers only — no zebra, no vertical grid lines
criteria.test: Rows are separated by horizontal dividers only (the border token) — no zebra striping, no vertical cell borders (bordered).

criteria.title: Behaviour matches DS V3 — sort arrow, filter popovers, freeze, pagination
criteria.test: Where present, behaviour matches DS V3: sort = a single directional arrow (not the dual caret); filter = the checklist (search + Reset/Apply) or Min/Max range popover; freeze = right-click, one column at a time, pinned leftmost with a shadow; pagination = brand-outlined active page + the "N / page" size changer.

criteria.title: Every icon is @phosphor-icons/react — never emoji
criteria.test: Every glyph (help, filter funnel, sort arrow, export, pin, drag handle) comes from @phosphor-icons/react as the DS table contract specifies; an emoji or a glyph from @ant-design/icons or another set fails.

criteria.title: Colour & radius come from tokens — no raw hex/px
criteria.test: Colour and radius in columns, cell renderers, rowClassName and the container bind to theme.useToken() / --aha-* and the radius scale — never a raw #hex, rgb() or magic px radius.

criteria.title: Cell padding is a live 16px — not collapsed to 0 by an undefined token
criteria.test: components.Table.cellPaddingBlock/Inline resolves to 16 (the literal 16 or token.size), not token.padding / paddingSM / paddingM, which are undefined in the AhaSlides token object and collapse the padding to 0.

targets.use: the DS Empty state
the DS Progress (role=progressbar + aria-value*)
the DS loading Skeleton
the DS Result page
the DS FieldError / FieldErrorDisplay
the DS LiveRegion
the DS a11y Progressbar wrapper
useIsMobile() / the DS viewport switch
the DS ErrorPage

criteria.title: Reaches for the canonical DS primitive, not a hand-rolled one
criteria.test: Every registry need is met by its DS primitive — field error → <aha-field-error>; announcement → <aha-live-region>; announced progress → <aha-progressbar>; mobile shape switch → useIsMobile() / <aha-viewport-switch>; full-page error → <aha-error-page>; empty state → <aha-empty>; loading → layout-mirroring <aha-skeleton>. A fresh reimplementation — even a correct one — FAILS.

criteria.title: Correct field-error variant, wired to its input
criteria.test: Forms use the default <aha-field-error> (a11y FieldError); respondent element renderers use variant="respondent" (FieldErrorDisplay: role=alert, aria-live=assertive). Either way the input sets aria-invalid and its aria-describedby points at the error's id (a DS <aha-input> forwards both). FAIL on the wrong variant or missing wiring.

criteria.title: Shape switches use useIsMobile(); styling uses @media (max-width: 767.98px)
criteria.test: A render that changes shape below 768px is gated on useIsMobile() / <aha-viewport-switch>; pure styling uses @media (max-width: 767.98px) directly. FAIL on an ad-hoc breakpoint, the hook driving pure styling, or a 768px / 767px media query.

criteria.title: Accessibility house rules honoured
criteria.test: The live region stays mounted when empty, is assertive + atomic and has no role=alert; an announced progress bar carries role=progressbar + aria-valuenow/min/max + aria-label; skeleton containers carry role=status + aria-busy; visible text uses DS / Typography text, not raw span/p; no state is conveyed by colour alone.

targets.use: the DS background rule: white by default, the sanctioned exceptions, and the one gradient allowed
the --aha-bg-* surface tokens every non-white background binds to

criteria.title: Every surface is white-by-default or a sanctioned exception
criteria.test: Cards, panels, page/section wrappers, modal/drawer bodies, table/list rows and tab panels are white or unset (--aha-bg-container) unless the non-white background is a sanctioned exception — a semantic feedback tint (--aha-bg-positive / -negative / -warning / -informative), the app-shell layout grey (--aha-bg-layout), an interactive hover/selected/active fill (--aha-bg-hover) — or the task carries explicit evidence the human asked for the colour; a decorative or brand tint on a neutral container fails here only.

criteria.title: No gradient as a background or fill
criteria.test: No linear-, radial- or conic-gradient is used as a background or fill; the only exception is the AI affordance, where the gradient sits on the border (border-box) and the padding-box fill stays white.

criteria.title: Non-white colour comes from a token, never a raw hex
criteria.test: A legitimately non-white surface takes its value from a DS token (--aha-bg-* / --aha-color-*), never a hardcoded #hex, rgb() or hsl() literal — a disallowed non-white surface is already a C1 fail and is not re-flagged here.

targets.use: the shared <aha-paywall>: popover anatomy, props, copy, analytics events and upgrade handler (C1–C7)

criteria.title: The gated affordance uses the shared Paywall component
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every pro-gated affordance wraps in `<Paywall>` (or uses `<PaywallCrownBadge>` as the anchor when the feature has no natural anchor). No hand-rolled upgrade modal, tooltip, or popover for monetisation — a bespoke upsell drifts from the presenter app's `UpgradePopover` and breaks the single-source-of-truth contract (PAYWALL-01).

criteria.title: Popover anatomy is exactly correct
criteria.test: **Rule.** The popover is, top to bottom: **crown badge** (the Vivid Pink circle custom `CrownBadge`, 16×16 SVG — *not* the generic Phosphor Crown) + **feature label**; then a **one-sentence value prop**; then the line **"Unlock with the _\<Plan\> plan_."** (plan name bold); then a **single** full-width (`block`) primary **Upgrade** CTA. No secondary "View plans" button, no dismiss link, no…

criteria.title: Props contract is honoured
criteria.test: **Rule.** `featureKey` is a stable `snake_case` token (e.g. `custom_survey_url`) reused across analytics and DOM hooks; `featureLabel` and `body` are present; `requiredPlan` is **one of `essential` | `pro`** (defaults to `pro`) — a real tier, not an invented plan name or a display string like "Pro plan" (PAYWALL-05, -07).

criteria.title: Copy rules are followed
criteria.test: **Rule.** **Feature label** is a short noun phrase (the locked feature's name), not a sentence. **Body** is exactly one sentence describing the *benefit* of unlocking (not "This is a Pro feature."), ending in a period.

criteria.title: The analytics contract is wired
criteria.test: **Rule.** `PAYWALL_SHOWN` fires when the popover opens and `PAYWALL_UPGRADE_CLICKED` fires when the CTA is clicked — each with props `{ feature: featureKey, plan: requiredPlan }`, and the click event fires **before** navigation or `onUpgrade` runs. Never gate a feature without both events; they are the funnel's denominator and conversion (PAYWALL-06).

criteria.title: Upgrade URL / handler behaviour is correct
criteria.test: **Rule.** The default CTA opens `UPGRADE_URL` (`https://ahaslides.com/pricing`) in a new tab with `noopener,noreferrer`, then closes the popover. When `onUpgrade` is provided it runs **instead** (analytics still fires first) and the popover still closes.

criteria.title: Crown-badge-only anchor used where the feature has no anchor
criteria.test: **Rule.** When a feature has no natural clickable anchor (e.g. a bare field label), the visible anchor is `<PaywallCrownBadge>`, which carries `role="img"` and an `aria-label` (default "Upgrade required").

targets.use: the status-pill pattern: dot + localised label, role=status, --{status} modifier colours
the DS status badge markup and status variants (C1, C2, C5)

criteria.title: The pill is a dot + a localised text label
criteria.test: **Rule.** A status pill is a single inline element containing a **dot** (`aha-status-pill__dot`) carrying the state colour **and** the visible **text label**. The dot is decorative; the text is the source of truth.

criteria.title: Markup uses the aha-status-pill / aha-status-pill--{status} convention
criteria.test: **Rule.** The base class is `aha-status-pill` plus a **per-state modifier** `aha-status-pill--{status}`, and the dot is `aha-status-pill__dot`. The state name comes from the status enum.

criteria.title: The role=status + aria-label accessibility contract is present
criteria.test: **Rule.** The element carries `role="status"` **and** an `aria-label` equal to the visible label, so the state is announced to assistive tech and **not conveyed by colour alone**. The text label is always present — the dot colour is never the sole carrier of meaning.

criteria.title: The label is sourced from i18n, never hardcoded
criteria.test: **Rule.** The visible label is always a translation lookup — ``t(`survey_status.${status}`)`` or the equivalent namespace for the object — never a hardcoded visible string. Adding a state means adding a translation key (and a `--{status}` modifier), not typing the word.

criteria.title: Colour comes from the --{status} modifier class, no inline hex
criteria.test: **Rule.** The **modifier class** — not an inline style or prop — drives the pill and dot colour, and it resolves to **semantic tokens**. Every state's colour lives in one stylesheet on tokens; the visible label is never coloured by a hardcoded hex.

targets.use: the settings pattern: naming, control choice, grouping by spacing, dependent and gated settings, danger zone, surface choice
the shared settings list, rows and groups (C4, C5, C9)

criteria.title: Setting names are noun phrases
criteria.test: Every setting name is a short noun phrase with no leading verb ("Enable", "Allow", "Turn on", "Show", "Toggle") and no trailing-sentence description. Group headers are noun phrases in sentence case with no colon or trailing punctuation.

criteria.title: Correct control — toggle vs checkbox, never mixed
criteria.test: A toggle for an immediate, independent binary; a checkbox for grouped/save-together options or consent (first person). Toggles and checkboxes are **not mixed within one group**.

criteria.title: Help text is the exception; explanation lives in a `?` tooltip
criteria.test: Always-visible help text appears **only** for a must-see consequence the user can't easily undo — one short sentence (≤90 chars), sentence case, ends with a period, states the consequence not the feature. All other elaboration is a `?` tooltip (≤140 chars, opens on hover **and** keyboard focus **and** tap, no links/buttons/ lists), or omitted.

criteria.title: Grouping & separation come from spacing — no dividers, no cards
criteria.test: Hierarchy and separation use `--aha-size*` spacing tokens (the monotonic 4/16/24/32/48 scale: 4 name→help, 16 sub-setting→parent, 24 between siblings, 32 between groups, 48 danger zone), **not** divider/rule lines and **not** raw px. Plain settings and groups are **never** wrapped in a card or **any container with its own background/tinted fill or border** — a lone toggle/setting row sits directly on the panel surface, not on a grey/tinted rounded pill.

criteria.title: Dependent sub-settings — hidden when parent off, nested when shown
criteria.test: A sub-setting that only applies when its parent is on is **hidden** when the parent is off (not shown disabled — unless the disabled state communicates an upgrade path). When shown, it reads as **nested under** its parent: indented 24px (`sizeLG`) with a 16px gap below the parent (`size`) **and de-emphasized** (label regular 400 in secondary text `--aha-text-secondary` #4A4A4A, where a top-level label is regular 400 in primary text #1A1A1A), and it is never bracketed by its own separators on both sides or…

criteria.title: Plan-gated settings are visible but locked
criteria.test: A setting requiring a plan the user isn't on stays **visible** (not hidden), shown locked with a crown badge that replaces its normal tooltip and opens the shared Paywall popover (owned by `aha-design-paywall` — one primary Upgrade CTA, not a bespoke two-CTA one). **FAIL** if a gated setting is hidden, or the badge opens a custom popover.

criteria.title: Dangerous settings — last, spacing-separated, danger Button, confirmed
criteria.test: Irreversible/destructive settings sit **last** (bottom of section or a Danger zone at panel bottom), set apart by the largest spacing gap (`sizeXXL`) — **not** a divider. The CTA is an AntD `danger` Button (`colorError`, no hardcoded hex); red is on the button only, never the label/toggle.

criteria.title: Correct surface — panel vs page vs modal vs drawer
criteria.test: Per-object/immediate-effect settings live in the inline editor **panel**; workspace/ account-scope in a **page**; one-time action config in a **modal**; medium-complexity supplements in a **drawer**. **FAIL** if a setting sits in the wrong surface for its scope (e.g.

criteria.title: Every object renders at its real height
criteria.test: No settings object holds space while rendering nothing visible: an empty section, an empty list wrapper inflating a parent's flex `gap`, or a plugin settings iframe reporting a non-zero height with an empty body / falling back to `height:100%`. An always-rendered wrapper around a conditional list renders only when the list is non-empty; a plugin settings iframe reports its height via…

criteria.title: Slide-type option list matches the "Items" component
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* The option list uses the reference row anatomy — drag handle (only when order matters) + text input + optional image button + **on-hover** delete — with a full-width **"+ Add"** button beneath and a `?`-tooltipped noun-phrase section label above. The text input shows a neutral placeholder when empty, a character counter **only on focus**, wraps to multiple lines, and…

criteria.title: Image support handled by the right component (per-option vs standalone field)
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* There are **two** image controls in the library, and the choice depends on whether the image is one cell of an option row or the field itself — using the wrong one (or hand-rolling either) is a FAIL.

criteria.title: Slide-type config follows the reference ordering
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* The panel is ordered **Question** (title + alignment + optional image + "Add description") → **option list** → **participation constraints** (placed right after the list) → **Time-limit toggle** revealing its duration select (dependent sub-setting) → **collapsed Advanced** section for low-frequency toggles. The standard sections (timing, show/hide results) are…

criteria.title: List wrapper matches the list shape (questions → QuestionList, item-groups → NumberedItem)
criteria.test: *(Slide-type config only.)* A repeatable settings list has **three** library wrappers, and the choice is fixed by the **shape of each item** — using the wrong one, or hand-rolling the accordion / number chip a shipped component already ships, is a FAIL (the list-shape sibling of C11's per-option-vs-standalone image choice): - **A flat set of answer choices for ONE question → `OptionRow`**. - **A list of QUESTIONS, each a prompt plus its own answer choices → `QuestionList`** (the collapsible question editor; it composes `NumberedItem` and `OptionRow`, never the reverse). - **A repeatable COMPOSITE item-group the creator counts by ordinal (a Card, a Round) → `NumberedItem`**. Also a FAIL: restyling or replacing the `NumberedItem` number chip — hiding or re-rendering it, or overriding the shadow part with `::part(chip)` (size, colour, ring, shadow) so it mirrors the canvas marker. The chip is the stock 22px muted-grey pill; the settings number is a plain ordinal and never mirrors the canvas marker. Drive it only through the real `n`, `label`, `variant`, `deletable` and `candelete` attributes.

criteria.title: Settings surface text is localised to the viewer's own app locale
criteria.test: *(Any settings surface that is localised at all — not gated to slide-type config; mark `N/A` only for a surface with no localisation.)* Settings/config text renders in the language of the **person viewing the settings surface**, not an unrelated content language. For a **slide-type plugin iframe** embedded in the AhaSlides presenter app, the right-panel SETTINGS/config text follows the…

criteria.title: No content-reset / restore-defaults control in a slide-type config panel
criteria.test: *(Slide-type right-panel config only — mark `N/A` for any other settings surface.)* A slide type's right-panel config **must not** carry a "Reset / Restore-defaults / Clear-all" control that re-seeds or wipes the **content the panel itself authors** — the dilemmas, items, buckets, lots or options the presenter typed. This is distinct from C7: C7 legitimises a genuine account/workspace…

criteria.title: Group title only over a real group, and no control in a group header
criteria.test: A setting-group / SectionHeader title is semibold and used **only** for a real group of two or more settings — never over a single field or a single list. The header and its action slot carry **no setting control** (no toggle, switch, input, select or button); a control is a settings item (label left, control right). Plain text such as a count may stay in the header. **FAIL** on a title over one field, or any control in the header.

criteria.title: Setting label weight and colour
criteria.test: A setting label (settings item / SettingRow / ModeField label) is regular 400 in primary text (`--aha-text-default` #1A1A1A). A label inside a sub-setting group is regular 400 in secondary text (`--aha-text-secondary` #4A4A4A). Sibling settings sit 24px apart. **FAIL** on a semibold setting label or a nested label in primary text.

targets.use: the feedback pattern: toast vs inline vs banner, correct/incorrect states, CSAT
the DS toast (C1)
the DS V3 <aha-alert> inline banner (C4)
the shared CSAT widget (C3)
the shared dismiss ✕ (C6)

criteria.title: Toasts are transient bottom-right pills — auto-dismiss, role=status, portalled
criteria.test: **Rule.** A toast is a **transient, non-actionable confirmation** ("Thanks for your feedback", "Copied"). It is a small `position: fixed` pill at the **viewport bottom-right** that rises from below (never shifting surrounding layout), **auto-dismisses after ~3s** with the timer **cleared on unmount**, carries **`role="status"`** (announced without stealing focus), and — because a `fixed` toast…

criteria.title: Inline correct/incorrect uses the a11y + semantic-token contract
criteria.test: **Rule.** Result feedback shown in place after an answer carries **`role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`** (informational, not urgent), and colours its container from **semantic tokens** — border `var(--aha-colorSuccess)` / `var(--aha-colorError)` and background `var(--aha-colorSuccessBg)` / `var(--aha-colorErrorBg)`, **never a hardcoded hex**. It leads with a strong correct/incorrect label…

criteria.title: CSAT uses the shared widget, a required source, and best-effort tracking
criteria.test: **Rule.** A satisfaction prompt uses the shared **`Csat`** widget — a binary thumbs rating with an optional follow-up on thumbs-down; **never** a bespoke rating control. It passes a **required `source`** token from the closed **`CsatSource`** union (one per placement) so Mixpanel gets stable, typo-proof segmentation; adding a placement means adding a union member.

criteria.title: Inline banners use the DS V3 Alert, not a bare AntD Alert
criteria.test: **Rule.** A persistent, in-context message the user may need to act on is a **Design System V3 Alert** — the DS `<aha-alert>` element (`contracts/alert.json`), **not** a bare `<Alert>` with default styling. Each of the five types — `success`, `error`, `info`, `warning`, `branding` — carries its DS `bg-surface` / `icon` token with no border **and a distinct glyph** (colour is never the only…

criteria.title: When NOT to use a toast is respected
criteria.test: **Rule.** A toast that auto-dismisses must **never** be the only place a required message lives. Route by situation: | Situation | Belongs in | |---|---| | Error the user must act on | inline **Alert** banner in context (C4) or an overlay Alert | | Field validation error | `FieldErrorDisplay` / a11y `FieldError` (shared-components) | | Destructive confirmation | a modal (`aha-design-overlays`) |…

criteria.title: One shared dismiss ✕ on banners, toasts, notifications and overlays
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every dismiss ✕ on an Alert, Info box, Background task, Toast, Notification, Modal or Drawer is the shared `tertiary icon-only <aha-button> (size xs)` (`contracts/button.json`): a 20 × 20 hit area (radius 6) with the 14px `system-x` glyph in #8A8A8A (`--aha-icon-muted`) that turns #1A1A1A (`--aha-text-default`) on a #F7F7F7 hover fill (`--aha-bg-hover`), top-pinned with its centre 2.5px above the first line's centre so it stays put when the text wraps, and 2px into the container's end padding (Info box: 15px from the right, 11px from the top). A sticky Toast takes it through `dismissibleToast`, a Notification through `dismissibleTitle` with `closable: false`. **FAIL** when any of these surfaces hand-rolls a ✕ (a bare `<button>×</button>`, an inline SVG, a raw icon with its own size or hover, a tertiary or 28 × 28 `<aha-button>` holding a 16px ✕, a circular ✕ — a disc, a 50% or pill radius, or `system-x-circle` used as a control rather than a status icon), shows antd's own message or notification close, or centres the ✕ on the whole card so it drifts down when the text wraps. Modal and Drawer carry it in the title through dismissibleModalTitle / dismissibleDrawerTitle with `closable={false}`. **N/A** when the material has no dismissible feedback surface.

targets.use: the overlay pattern: surface choice, dismiss safety, state reset, async confirm, inline errors
the DS Modal (C1, C3, C5, C7)
the DS Drawer — right placement, responsive width (C4)
the DS Popover (C1)

criteria.title: The right surface is chosen — modal vs drawer vs popover
criteria.test: **Rule.** The surface fits the job: a **modal** for a focused, blocking decision or short flow (confirmations, destructive actions, one-time config); a **drawer** for a detail view or medium-complexity panel that supplements the page (a record's report, distribution settings); a **popover** for a small, anchored, contextual snippet (quick info, a compact input, an upsell) — never for a…

criteria.title: Dismiss behaviour is safety-critical
criteria.test: **Rule.** **Destructive / data-loss overlays MUST NOT dismiss on outside/mask click** — set `mask={{ closable: false }}` so a stray backdrop click can't trigger destruction, leaving `keyboard` (Esc) and the explicit **X** button as the only dismiss paths. Non-destructive overlays may allow mask-close.

criteria.title: State resets between opens
criteria.test: **Rule.** The overlay sets `destroyOnHidden` (Modal) / `destroyOnClose` (Drawer) so transient state — form input, error text, busy flag — resets between opens. If the instance can stay mounted, local error and busy state are also cleared explicitly on open rather than relying on unmount alone.

criteria.title: Drawers use placement=right and responsive width
criteria.test: **Rule.** Drawers default to `placement="right"` with **responsive width** `width={isMobile ? '100%' : <fixed>}` (e.g. `720`) driven by `useIsMobile()` — full-bleed on mobile, fixed panel on desktop.

criteria.title: Async confirm follows the busy-guard / await / stay-open pattern
criteria.test: **Rule.** When `onConfirm` returns a promise, the overlay: (1) guards re-entry (`if (busy) return`), sets `busy`, clears prior error; (2) `await`s the action; (3) on rejection **stays open** and surfaces the error inline (see C6), then clears `busy`; (4) on success the caller closes the overlay. Never close a destructive overlay before its action resolves, and never fire-and-forget.

criteria.title: Errors surface inline, never a nested modal
criteria.test: **Rule.** Failures are surfaced **inside** the overlay with an inline **DS V3 Alert** (`AhaAlert type="error"` — the banner component owned by [[aha-design-feedback]], **not** a bare AntD `<Alert>` with default styling). This judge owns *placement* (error goes inline, overlay stays open); feedback owns the Alert's *styling*.

criteria.title: Destructive confirm uses a danger-styled button
criteria.test: **Rule.** A destructive confirmation uses `okButtonProps={{ danger: true, type: 'primary', loading: busy }}` — the **dark danger styling lives on the action button**, never on the title or body — and Cancel, the safe choice, is the primary button (`cancelButtonProps={{ type: 'primary', disabled: busy }}`), disabled while busy. For confirmations the title is a **question** ("Delete this survey permanently?").

targets.use: the presenter-canvas pattern: framed vs full-canvas, declared actions, deck ink and fonts
the colour and type tokens every hard-coded colour/font check binds to (C1, C2)

criteria.title: No hard-coded colours or fonts
criteria.test: **Rule.** All colour and font values come from xprops: - `xprops.slide.baseColour`, `xprops.slide.textColour`, `xprops.slide.backgroundImage` - `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` - `xprops.presentationColorPalette[n]`, `xprops.presentationLighterColorPalette[n]`

criteria.title: Semantic state colours applied to the indicator, NOT the chart
criteria.test: **Two different colour jobs on a canvas — keep them separated:**

criteria.title: Action buttons in the right place: declared for the host bar on a built plugin, in-canvas on the Developer Platform
criteria.test: **Rule.** On a **built** slide plugin, Previous / Next / Summarise / Reset and any other slide-specific actions are **declared** via the plugin manifest's `actions` array and **painted by the host** in the presenter control bar (`PresenterControlBarNew.vue`, region `ncb-center` portal, rendered through `NcbPluginActions.vue`); that canvas iframe never contains the action buttons themselves. A **build-less Developer Platform** slide type (presenter.html / audience.html / settings.html loading `lib/all.js`) has no manifest actions: its presenter controls render **inside** the canvas as DS `<aha-button>` elements (sized by C17) — that placement PASSes here, and a raw `<button>` there FAILs.

criteria.title: Action shape correct, with sensible variant hierarchy
criteria.test: **Rule.** A built slide plugin does NOT pick a button size — the host renders every declared action via the `<aha-antd-button>` design-system wrapper at whatever size the host configures; the plugin's job is to declare the right **data** (label, variant hierarchy with ≤1 primary, boolean disabled/loading). On the Developer Platform the same variant hierarchy applies to the in-canvas `<aha-button>` row.

criteria.title: Legible against the REAL background — WCAG AA contrast, readable size, AND real text
criteria.test: Three failure axes, one goal: the slide is read from a distance, so meaningful text and shapes must **contrast enough**, be **big enough**, AND **read as normal running text** (not a decorative treatment) to be understood from the worst seat. Any one axis failing → C5 FAIL.

criteria.title: Non-colour cue paired with every colour-bearing signal
criteria.test: **Rule.** If colour carries meaning (right/wrong, winner/loser, warning/normal, correct/incorrect), it MUST be paired with at least one of: - An **icon** (✓, ✗, crown, alert) — **preferred**: compact, language-neutral - A **label** ("Correct", "Incorrect", "Winner") — heavier, brings an i18n surface - A **shape** (border style, pattern, outline) - **Position** (winner = top of list)

criteria.title: Framed vs full-canvas chosen intentionally in the manifest
criteria.test: **Rule.** The plugin's manifest declares `setting.enableFullScreen` explicitly: - **Framed** (`setting.enableFullScreen: false`): host renders the question title / description / question image at the top of the stage; the canvas iframe only renders the answer/interaction area. - **Full-canvas** (`setting.enableFullScreen: true`): host hides its chrome; the canvas iframe renders its own title and…

criteria.title: Plugin initialises its locale from `presentation.language` xprop
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every user-visible string passes through i18n. The plugin runs in its own iframe with **its own i18n instance** — it does NOT inherit the host's locale state.

criteria.title: Visual restraint — no AI-generated design tells
criteria.test: Five specific choices make a canvas read as machine-generated — or plain broken — rather than designed. **Any one → FAIL.**

criteria.title: Keyboard-shortcut affordances
criteria.test: **Scope.** This criterion is about controls the **canvas renders itself** — a bespoke overlay the host control bar (NCB, §C3) doesn't paint: an animated game's play / pause, a reveal toggle, a music-mute button, a settings popover. Host-painted NCB actions get their shortcut chips, focus order, and sound from the host and are out of scope here.

criteria.title: Deck-ink fallback reads on the surface it lands on
criteria.test: **Scope.** Ink written as `xprops.slide.textColour ?? <fallback>` (or `textColour || …`). The default deck leaves `slide.textColour` **unset** — the host paints body text itself and forwards nothing — so the fallback is the **real paint path on the most common deck**, not an edge case.

criteria.title: Full-canvas slide renders the host title itself
criteria.test: **Scope.** Fires only when the manifest declares `setting.enableFullScreen: true` (full-canvas). A **framed** slide (`enableFullScreen: false`) PASSes vacuously — the host draws the title bar, so the canvas must not.

criteria.title: On-canvas text clears a legible size floor
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every meaningful on-canvas text — the title / question, answer text, data values, status lines, option labels — uses a **fixed-px type-scale role at or above the 16px caption floor**, the same scale C5 defines (no new number is introduced here): | role | class | px @720 | |---|---|---| | caption (floor) | `text-base` | 16 | | body (default) | `text-lg` | 18 | | subhead | `text-2xl` |…

criteria.title: Deck font is LOADED into the iframe, not just referenced
criteria.test: **Scope.** Fires whenever the canvas renders text in the deck font — it binds `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` (directly, or via a `deckFont` computed) to an element's `font-family`. A canvas that renders no text, or renders only in the bundled default face, PASSes vacuously.

criteria.title: Canvas content is padded, not clipped by an under-padded container
criteria.test: **Rule.** Meaningful content — a title, a progress / "rung" badge (`RUNG 1 OF 4`, `Q1 of 5`), a status line, the first row of a list — must sit inside adequate container padding and render **fully visible**. Nothing important is sliced by an under-padded container, an `overflow`-bounded box, or a flex column that squeezes or overflows its top item.

criteria.title: A per-round advance stepper uses the default (secondary) variant, never the primary accent
criteria.test: **Rule.** A slide action the presenter clicks to advance **one step at a time through many rounds** — This or That's *Next pair*, a per-question *Next*, a dilemma ladder's *Next dilemma / rung* — is workhorse NAVIGATION, not a climactic CTA. It MUST take the **default / secondary** variant (the solid white-background button), never the filled **primary** accent — and that holds in **both**…

criteria.title: An in-canvas presenter control is <aha-button> sized by attribute (size="xl"), never resized through ::part
criteria.test: *(Fires when the canvas renders its own presenter controls — the Developer Platform's in-canvas row or a built plugin's fallback. N/A otherwise.)* Each control is a DS `<aha-button>` whose size comes from the `size` attribute — `size="xl"` (52px) for controls the room reads from a distance. Any `::part(button)` rule (or inline style) that sets height, padding, font-size or radius FAILs, as does recolouring through `::part` or a per-slide accent variable instead of `--aha-color-primary`.

criteria.title: A framed slide over a photo keeps the deck showing — no slide-wide scrim
criteria.test: *(Fires on a framed slide — `enableFullScreen: false` — rendered with `slide.backgroundImage` set. N/A otherwise.)* The root and the whole answer area stay transparent. A scrim, panel or backdrop painted behind the entire board (e.g. an `#app.scrim` class added whenever a background image is set) FAILs. Only bounded surfaces may be opaque: cards, chips, or a small caption bar behind a single line of text that needs contrast.

criteria.title: One accent per deck — palette[0] on --aha-color-primary, same on every surface
criteria.test: The deck accent is `presentationColorPalette[0]` published as `--aha-color-primary` on `:root` (with the `--aha-button-primary-*` hover / press / text tokens), so canvas, audience and every `<aha-button>` show the same colour. FAIL when a surface recomputes the accent (mixes it toward the ink until a contrast target, darkens it in steps, uses a 'towardInk' variant for selection), when two surfaces show different 'primary' colours, or when a semantic colour (success teal, error red) is used as a data / series / column colour. Picking only the LABEL ink by contrast is correct.

criteria.title: Borders are hairlines and radius follows the DS scale
criteria.test: A bounded white card has a 1px neutral border (`--aha-border-default` #E3E3E3) and 12px radius (`--aha-radius-lg`); a deck-owned surface (chip, field, track) a 1px `currentColor` 10% hairline, no 20% exception; dashed empty states 1px; option tiles, inputs and buttons 8px. FAIL on 2px (or heavier) outlines on cards, tiles, chips or inputs, on borders at heavy ink (e.g. 14–55% textColour at 2px), or on a rectangular container above 12px radius.

criteria.title: One fixed dark ink: #1A1A1A
criteria.test: Wherever the slide uses a fixed dark ink (labels on a light fill, the dark half of a contrast pick, a fallback ink), it is `--aha-text-default` #1A1A1A. FAIL on the retired indigo `#1A1A2E` used as text ink, or on a second near-black (`#000`, `#111`) used alongside it.

criteria.title: Interactive states animate with motion tokens on persistent nodes
criteria.test: Every hover, selected, expanded or revealed state transitions with `--aha-motion-*` durations and `--aha-ease-*` curves (no bare `.2s` literals), declared on nodes that persist across updates. FAIL when interactive states snap (no transition at all), or when the view is rebuilt with `innerHTML =` / `replaceChildren()` on each state change so the transition can never fire.

criteria.title: Stage steppers and comboboxes are the DS elements, current stage in ink
criteria.test: *(Fires when the canvas shows a stage / round indicator or a type-to-pick field. N/A otherwise.)* A stage indicator is `<aha-stepper>` (size="lg" on the canvas, `color` set to the deck ink) and a type-to-pick field is `<aha-autocomplete>`, both from `lib/all.js`. FAIL on hand-rolled stepper pills (`.step` spans / `<li>`s styled per slide) or a hand-built `<input>` + `<ul>` suggestion list, and FAIL when the current stage is filled or outlined with the primary accent (`--aha-color-primary`, palette[0]) — the accent belongs to the one action that advances the flow; the current stage is marked with ink.

targets.use: the audience-screen pattern: mobile-first column, self-rendered states, deck-tracking controls, text economy
the colour and type tokens every hard-coded colour/font check binds to (C1, C2)

criteria.title: No hard-coded colours or fonts
criteria.test: **Rule.** All colour and font values come from xprops: - `xprops.slide.textColour` - `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` - `xprops.presentationColorPalette[n]`, `xprops.presentationLighterColorPalette[n]`

criteria.title: Semantic state colours bundled, applied to the indicator
criteria.test: **Rule.** Meaning-bearing state colours (correct/incorrect, success/error, submission feedback, validation) must come from the plugin's own **bundled** design-system tokens. They do NOT come from: - The deck's palette (`xprops.presentationColorPalette[n]`) — a palette may not contain a usable red/green, so state would silently shift per deck.

criteria.title: Mobile-first single column + height reported via onHeightChange
criteria.test: **Rule.** The audience layout must be: - **Single column.** No side-by-side panels assuming desktop width. - **Fluid up to host's max-width** (host enforces ~710–840px in framed mode); no fixed device-width assumptions.

criteria.title: Plugin self-renders submitted / waiting / correct-incorrect; host utilities used where they fit
criteria.test: **Rule.** For built-in slide types the host overlays a "Waiting…" screen after submit. **Plugins do not get that** — the iframe stays mounted and the plugin must render the post-submission UX itself: - **Just submitted** — ✓ confirmation rendered inside the iframe - **Waiting for the next slide** — same surface, calm hold state - **Quiz correct/incorrect** — state colour on indicator (icon), bar…

criteria.title: WCAG AA contrast + touch targets + mobile readability
criteria.test: **Rule.** Three thresholds on the audience surface: **Contrast** — every meaningful text and shape meets WCAG AA against the **plugin-chosen background**: - 4.5:1 floor for text (3:1 for large text ≥18pt / 14pt bold) - 3:1 floor for meaningful non-text shapes (bar fills, status dots, dividers)

criteria.title: Non-colour cue paired with every colour-bearing signal
criteria.test: **Rule.** If colour carries meaning (right/wrong, correct/incorrect, submission state, leader/winner), it MUST be paired with at least one non-colour cue. **Prefer icon** as the cue — compact, language-neutral.

criteria.title: Framed vs full-canvas declared explicitly in the manifest
criteria.test: **Rule.** The plugin manifest declares `setting.enableFullScreen` explicitly: - **Framed** (`setting.enableFullScreen: false`) — host renders question image, title, description, audio button, countdown progress *above* the iframe. The audience iframe owns the answer area only.

criteria.title: Plugin i18n initialised from xprops.presentation.language
criteria.test: **Rule.** The audience iframe has **its own i18n instance** (separate document, separate bundle). It does NOT inherit the host's locale state.

criteria.title: Submit button matches the standard spec
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every built-in audience slide type uses one consistent submit-button look + behaviour (the host design system's `aha-antd-button` in the "primary-alt" variant). That component doesn't cross the iframe boundary, so plugin authors build their own — but the in-iframe button MUST match the shared spec (visual + behaviour + wiring), or audience experience drifts per slide type.

criteria.title: Visual restraint — no AI-generated design tells
criteria.test: Three specific choices make the audience UI read as machine-generated. **Any one → FAIL.**

criteria.title: Transform / animation stays inside the reported box
criteria.test: **Rule.** `onHeightChange` reports the plugin's **resting** box, and the host shrink-wraps the iframe to that height, painting nothing outside it. Any transform that lifts content past the reported edges — a swipe tilt, a drag ghost, a hover pop, a settle bounce (`rotate`, `translateY(-n)`, `scale(>1)`) — gets **clipped by the iframe**.

criteria.title: Swipe / drag gesture stays smooth (60 fps)
criteria.test: **Rule.** A card the audience drags or flings re-renders every frame while it moves. Two things reliably make that laggy on a real phone, and both are FAILs: 1.

criteria.title: Text economy — no redundant text; instructions are unboxed body text
criteria.test: **Rule.** Every word on the audience surface must add information the controls don't, and instructions stay quiet. Two facets: 1.

criteria.title: Host-owned transient notices not re-rendered in the iframe
criteria.test: **Rule.** The host owns two round-end announcements; the plugin must not duplicate either inside the iframe (framed mode).

criteria.title: Shared components used, not rebuilt
criteria.test: **Rule.** Where the repo ships an audience component library, the surface is built FROM it. A control that duplicates a library component's job FAILs — and it FAILs even when it renders identically today, because the library is where the cross-cutting guarantees live in one place: ink that tracks the deck, the frosted surface that survives a photographic deck, the touch-target floor, the…

criteria.title: Deck font is LOADED into the iframe, not just referenced
criteria.test: **Scope.** Fires whenever the audience surface renders text in the deck font — it binds `xprops.presentation.fontFamily` (directly, or via a `deckFont` computed, or a global `font-family: inherit` that ultimately resolves to it) to its text. A surface that renders only in the bundled default face PASSes vacuously.

criteria.title: Selection controls and the "your pick" indicator track the deck
criteria.test: **Rule.** The controls that carry choice and selection — a Radio, a Checkbox, and the ring/edge that marks the row a participant picked — must read from the deck, not from a fixed brand colour. Two facets, both reported (AHAM-701): 1.

criteria.title: A filled slider / progress track carries a deck-ink edge
criteria.test: **Rule.** A slider's FILLED (accent) portion, and a progress fill, must carry the SAME deck-ink hairline the empty rail already has, so a coloured fill does not sink into a same-hue deck (AHAM-701 issue 4). The edge is the deck ink at the shared audience border alpha (10%, one value for every audience border and track), reached through `currentColor` so it tracks the deck — the same edge the unfilled rail uses, extended onto the fill.

criteria.title: Body copy and option labels use the audience default body size
criteria.test: **Rule.** Primary body text, answer-option labels, chip labels and tags render at the audience DEFAULT body size, 16px (`--aha-size-l`) (AHAM-701 issue 2). 14px (`--aha-size-default`) is legitimate ONLY on secondary metadata — a vote-count chip, a percentage, a character counter — never on the option label or main body copy. **Token trap:** `--aha-size-sm` is **12px**, not the 14px 'text-sm', so primary copy bound to `--aha-size-sm` FAILs even though the name reads 'small text'.

criteria.title: A horizontal slider's rail sits flush with its end labels
criteria.test: **Rule.** A horizontal audience slider's rail runs edge-to-edge inside its container, aligned flush under its min/max end labels — no leftover Ant component margin (e.g. a default `margin: 10px 6px`-ish inset) shifting the rail inward so it no longer lines up with the captions it belongs to (AHAM-701 issue 3).

criteria.title: Distinct labelled sections are separated by ≥24px
criteria.test: **Rule.** An audience screen that stacks two or more DISTINCT labelled sections — a section being a heading/label plus the control group it introduces, e.g. `Choose a lot` + the answer options, then `Set your bid` + the slider — puts at least **24px** of vertical space between one section and the next (AHAM-701 issue).

criteria.title: A repeated row holds its DECLARED range, in one shape, with no fixed void
criteria.test: **Rule.** A row that repeats — an item plus its control — is designed for the whole range of content it is *allowed* to hold, not for the content it happened to be posed with. Three things follow, and each one is a way the same design fails.

criteria.title: Participant identity shown only when the slide opts into the host join flow
criteria.test: **Rule.** The audience iframe never knows the participant's own name, emoji or team unless the slide type opts into the host's join/identity flow. The host populates `audienceName` / `audienceEmoji` (and team) ONLY when the manifest declares `setting.enableAudienceJoinPresentation: true` — that flag is what makes the host run the QR/join step and hand the identity down.

criteria.title: A form field sits on a chosen legible surface with deck-tracking ink
criteria.test: **Rule.** An audience `<input>` / `<textarea>` / `<select>` is a *bounded field* the participant has to find and read their own typing in — it needs an explicitly chosen surface and ink, not the defaults it inherits. C5 says the plugin picks its own background *in general*; this criterion makes that testable for FORM FIELDS specifically, because the two ways a field goes wrong are both invisible…

criteria.title: A Select / dropdown popup opens below, themes its panel, and stays in the iframe box
criteria.test: **Rule.** A native `<select>` or a custom popup menu (an Ant `Select`, a combobox) has a second surface — the open PANEL — that the closed control's styling does not cover. Three things must hold, and each is a separate way the same control fails: **a.

criteria.title: Exactly one instruction line per audience screen — a second, restating line FAILs
criteria.test: **Rule.** An audience screen carries at most ONE instruction line telling the participant what to do. A second line — a separate instruction elsewhere on the screen, or an inner prompt / placeholder / hint beside the control — that RESTATES the same task is redundant: it says nothing the first line didn't, and on the shrink-wrapped mobile surface two instructions compete for the eye and push the…

criteria.title: A full SubmittedCard is only for a swipe-card interaction; every other slide locks its answer in place
criteria.test: **Rule.** The separate, full-surface `SubmittedCard` component — the one that REPLACES the whole answer surface with a standalone "you're in" card — is only appropriate for a **swipe-card interaction**: a slide where the participant's answer IS a card they swipe or tap (true-or-false's swipe/tap-a-card, this-or-that, and the like). There the card is the mechanic, so swapping to a submitted card…

criteria.title: An audience text field's LABEL tracks the deck ink at the 16px body size
criteria.test: **Rule.** The label ABOVE an audience `<input>` / `<textarea>` ("Your answer", "Your name", …) is read against the DECK, not against the field's own chosen surface — so it obeys the same two rules the deck body copy does, and the two defaults it inherits from Ant's `Form.Item` label both break it: **a. The label tracks the deck ink.** The label colour is `xprops.slide.textColour`, NOT a fixed…

criteria.title: A field's character counter sits INSIDE it, reveals on focus, counts DOWN, in muted field ink
criteria.test: **Rule.** A character counter on an audience `<input>` / `<textarea>` mirrors the shipped settings `CountedTextarea` / `CountedInput` pattern — four things, and each has a specific wrong default that this criterion catches: **a. Inside the field, not below it.** The counter is positioned INSIDE the field box — bottom-right for a `<textarea>`, right-aligned for a single-line `<input>` — not on a…

criteria.title: An ACTIVE audience submit button is passed the deck accent, not left on the component's purple fallback
criteria.test: **Rule.** This repo's submit CTA is the shared library component (`SubmitButton` / `AudienceSubmitButton` from `@/iframe/audience`), whose fill DEFAULTS to the fixed brand purple and only tracks the deck when it is passed `:accent="presentationColorPalette[0]"`. So an ACTIVE (answerable) submit button MUST bind that accent.

criteria.title: One accent per deck — the same --aha-color-primary as the canvas
criteria.test: The selected chip, checked control and submit fill use `presentationColorPalette[0]` published as `--aha-color-primary` on `:root` — the same value the presenter canvas uses. FAIL when the audience recomputes the accent (a 'towardInk' selection colour beside a raw submit colour), when two controls on one screen show different 'primary' colours, or when a semantic colour (success teal, error red) is used as a data or column colour. Picking only the label ink by contrast is correct.

criteria.title: Borders are hairlines and radius follows the DS scale
criteria.test: A bounded white card has a 1px `--aha-border-default` (#E3E3E3) border and 12px radius; a deck chip a 1px 10% ink border; option tiles, inputs and the submit button 8px. FAIL on 2px (or heavier) outlines at heavy ink (e.g. 55% textColour) on chips, cards or inputs, or on a rectangular container above 12px radius.

criteria.title: One fixed dark ink: #1A1A1A
criteria.test: Any fixed dark ink — a label on a light accent, a fallback ink — is `--aha-text-default` #1A1A1A. FAIL on the retired indigo `#1A1A2E` as text ink, or `#000` as the dark label on the accent.

criteria.title: Interactive states animate with motion tokens on persistent nodes
criteria.test: Hover, selected, pressed and expanded states transition with `--aha-motion-*` durations and `--aha-ease-*` curves on nodes that persist. FAIL when states snap with no transition, use a bare duration literal, or when the screen is rebuilt with `innerHTML =` on each change so the transition never fires.

criteria.title: Stage steppers and comboboxes are the DS elements, current stage in ink
criteria.test: *(Fires when the audience screen shows a stage indicator or a type-to-pick field. N/A otherwise.)* On the Developer Platform a stage indicator is `<aha-stepper>` and a type-to-pick field (owner, name) is `<aha-autocomplete size="large">`, both from `lib/all.js`. FAIL on a hand-rolled stepper or a hand-built `<input>` + suggestion list / custom `<div role="listbox">`, and FAIL when the current stage is painted with the primary accent instead of ink.

targets.use: the <aha-chart> chart types, the palette attribute (brand | deck) and the chart types it does not ship

criteria.title: A result/data chart is <aha-chart>, not a hand-rolled or third-party chart
criteria.test: Every result or data chart on an app screen, Report, canvas or audience view is rendered with the DS `<aha-chart>` element for a chart type its live contract ships. A hand-rolled SVG/canvas/CSS-bar chart, or a third-party chart library (Chart.js, Recharts, ECharts, D3-drawn, Highcharts, ApexCharts, Victory, Nivo), fails. The one exception is `@ant-design/plots` for a chart type `<aha-chart>` does not ship.

criteria.title: <aha-chart> uses the palette for its surface
criteria.test: App screens such as Report use `palette="brand"` (the default); the presenting or audience canvas uses `palette="deck"` with the deck's `colors` and `ink`. A canvas chart left on the brand palette, or an app-screen chart painted with hand-picked series colours, fails.
